          Privacy first

          Your prompts and code never leave your machine: all optimization runs locally.

          Headroom compresses the noise reversibly, so the model still reaches anything it needs, with no measurable hit to output quality.

        
      

    

  

  
    
      The problem

      You hit your limit before you finish the work

      
        Claude Code and ChatGPT Codex are the best part of your week, until the usage runs out. Most of what
        burns through that limit isn't your thinking; it's the noise your tools pump into every prompt.
        Upgrading a tier only raises the ceiling: you send the same bloated prompts and burn through the
        bigger limit too.
      

    

  

  
  
    How it works

    Local input compression

    Headroom compresses repetitive tool output and context locally before forwarding requests to your coding agent's AI provider. Stored originals remain available through retrieval tools. Savings depend on the content processed.

      Add-ons

      Optional tools for the waste compression can't reach

      
        Core compression works on its own. These install with one click from the app and go after the
        rest: noisy command output, binary documents, whole-file reads, and long-winded replies.
      

    


    
      
        Terminal

        RTK

        Summarizes supported terminal-command output instead of forwarding the whole dump.

      


      
        Documents

        MarkItDown

        Converts PDF and Office documents to Markdown, so your agent can read them at all.

      


      
        Code

        Serena

        Symbol lookup and targeted reads, so a question about one function doesn't pull the whole file.

      


      
        Code

        Codebase Memory

        Indexes repository structure and relationships, so the agent stops re-deriving your layout.

      


      
        Docs

        Context7

        Retrieves version-specific library documentation instead of guessing at an API.

      


      
        Output

        Ponytail

        Adds instructions that steer the model toward smaller, simpler implementations.

      


      
        Output

        Caveman

        Adds instructions for shorter replies, which cuts output tokens on every turn.
